name: W*nder
dek: A CBD brand site that teaches before it sells.

at_a_glance.role: Sole UX/UI designer, end to end
at_a_glance.scope: Competitor analysis, flows, design system, hi-fi UI, usability scenarios
at_a_glance.hard_part: Selling a product some visitors still associate with a stigma, where every screen has to earn trust before it can ask for a purchase.
at_a_glance.look_for: How lab-test transparency is treated as a first-class navigation destination, not a compliance footnote.

problem.claim_h2: You cannot sell CBD to someone who does not trust it
problem.thesis: For a first-time CBD buyer, the real barrier is not price or flavor, it is doubt, so the site has to educate and prove safety before it pitches.
problem.body: W*nder is a sparkling CBD beverage brand built around transparency, with every batch tested by an independent lab. The site's job was to turn that testing into something a hesitant visitor can actually find, read, and believe.
bullets: Lab results on competitor sites are buried or missing, so shoppers cannot verify what they are drinking.
New users lack basic education on what CBD is, what it does, and whether it is safe.
Lingering cannabis stigma means conventional weed-adjacent branding actively undermines credibility.
problem.research_note: Desk research compared Charlotte's Web, Medterra, and Joy Organics on lab-result transparency, educational depth, and navigation clarity to locate the gaps W*nder could own.

design.claim_h2: Proof, then education, then the sale
design.intro: The homepage and lab-results page run the same sequence: a warm, un-cannabis identity up front, evidence in the middle, and every call to action pointing toward learning or verifying before buying.

figures.caption: The hero leads with the four cans and a plain-language promise; Drink Up is the only CTA, so the first read stays uncluttered.
figures.alt: W*nder homepage hero with four brightly colored CBD cans floating around the headline Works like a w*nder and a Drink Up button.

figures.caption: Dosage and purity sit in circled callouts beside a See the Proof CTA, turning the trust claim into a link a skeptic can follow.
figures.alt: Trust section with the headline Trust us, it works, circular badges for CBD content, zero THC, and purity, and a See the Proof button.

figures.caption: Repeating We know CBD in four type treatments sets up the beginner's question and routes it to the education page, not the shop.
figures.alt: Educational section with the phrase We know CBD stacked in four typographic styles next to the question But what exactly is it and a Get to Know CBD button.

figures.caption: The 420 Rule gives the brand a social mission tied to cannabis prohibition, with a restrained leaf mark that avoids weed-culture cliches.
figures.alt: Brand mission section titled The 420 Rule with copy about reinvesting profits in affected communities and a green cannabis leaf inside a thin circle.

figures.caption: The lab-results page opens by naming the industry's problem, the wild west of CBD, so publishing every batch reads as the answer.
figures.alt: Lab results page hero on a burnt orange background with outlined type asking Is your CBD legitimate and safe and the subhead It's the wild west in CBD.

figures.caption: Every variant carries its own View Test link, so proof is per product, one click from the can, not a generic quality page.
figures.alt: Four W*nder can variants in orange, yellow, green, and navy, each with a View Test link underneath.

flows: Check what a batch is tested for
Pick a variant for your need
validation.honest_line: Moderated scenarios were scripted around a skeptical first-time buyer moving from doubt to purchase, but as a concept project the board records the test design rather than measured outcomes, so it shows how trust would be evaluated, not that it was won.

appendix.framing: The system underneath the pages: a palette built to feel calm rather than clinical, and the grid that keeps educational content readable.

figures.caption: Blue Metallic, Bronze Satin, and Viridis ramps in eight steps each give the warm-but-credible range every section draws from.
figures.alt: Color sheet showing the Squid's Ink primary and three secondary ramps, Blue Metallic, Bronze Satin, and Viridis, each in eight tonal steps with hex values, plus neutrals.

figures.caption: A 12-column desktop grid with generous margins keeps long educational copy from sprawling edge to edge.
figures.alt: Grid system spec for a 1440px desktop layout showing 12 pink columns with labeled margin, column, and gutter widths.
